themes.title: Transnational Recalibration Following MAGA Midterm Defeats
themes.blurb: The fallout from the US midterm election losses has triggered global waves of strategic distancing, internal blame, and ideological reassessment across right-wing parties. Leaders and factions across Europe and Latin America are digesting the political shift, with figures like Nigel Farage and JD Vance pointing to foreign interventionism while European allies adjust their rhetoric.

countries.note: Internal Republican blame game erupts as lawmakers cite the Iran conflict and cost-of-living issues for congressional defeats.

countries.name: 🇬🇧 Reform UK

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega

countries.name: 🇧🇷 Bolsonarismo / Partido Liberal

countries.note: Internal party disputes flare regarding AfD's long-term positioning alongside Trump's political movement.

themes.blurb: Populist and right-wing figures are building direct cross-border ties to project ideological alignment and bypass official diplomatic channels. High-profile meetings between Argentine President Javier Milei and Vox leadership in Spain, alongside Bolsonarists gathering at Mar-a-Lago, demonstrate active transnational networking.

themes.title: National Priority Rhetoric and Hardline Migration Demands
themes.blurb: Right-wing parties across Europe are ramping up pressure to restrict foreign development aid, curb migration, and mandate national preference in local governance. From Vox demanding 'national priority' clauses in Spanish regional budgets to Reform UK and Rassemblement National pushing hardline policy demands, fiscal nationalism remains key.
